title: S&P 500 Total Return Index (^SP500TR) daily price history
notes: Series for the `sp500` benchmark. Fiscal-year total return computed as the ratio of the last observation on or before June 30 of the fiscal year to the last observation on or before June 30 of the prior fiscal year, minus 1. Dividends are reinvested (index level is itself total return). The total-return version of the S&P 500, so the index level already includes reinvested dividends; the price-only ^GSPC would understate returns by roughly 2pp a year.

title: Vanguard Total Bond Market Index Fund Investor Shares (VBMFX) daily price history
notes: Series for the `us_aggregate_bond` benchmark. Fiscal-year total return computed as the ratio of the last observation on or before June 30 of the fiscal year to the last observation on or before June 30 of the prior fiscal year, minus 1. Dividends are reinvested (adjusted close). Stands in for the Bloomberg US Aggregate Bond Index, which is not freely redistributable. Chosen over the BND ETF because BND only launched in 2007 and this fund's history reaches 1986, covering the full FY2000-FY2025 window on one consistent basis.

title: Vanguard Total International Stock Index Fund Investor Shares (VGTSX) daily price history
notes: Series for the `intl_equity` benchmark. Fiscal-year total return computed as the ratio of the last observation on or before June 30 of the fiscal year to the last observation on or before June 30 of the prior fiscal year, minus 1. Dividends are reinvested (adjusted close). Developed plus emerging markets combined, matching how the `intl_public_equity` allocation category is defined. Chosen over the VXUS ETF (2011) and EFA (2001) for full FY2000-FY2025 coverage.

title: Vanguard Real Estate Index Fund Investor Shares (VGSIX) daily price history
notes: Series for the `reit` benchmark. Fiscal-year total return computed as the ratio of the last observation on or before June 30 of the fiscal year to the last observation on or before June 30 of the prior fiscal year, minus 1. Dividends are reinvested (adjusted close). Listed US REITs. Chosen over the VNQ ETF (2004) for full FY2000-FY2025 coverage. Note this is listed real estate only -- it does not represent the direct real estate, timber and energy holdings that make up much of an endowment's real-assets sleeve, which is an honesty note task 1.7 must carry.

title: 3-Month Treasury Bill Secondary Market Rate, Discount Basis (TB3MS)
publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, via FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)
notes: Series for the `cash` benchmark. FRED publishes an annualized monthly rate, not a return series, so the fiscal-year return is computed by compounding the twelve monthly rates from July of the prior year through June: prod(1 + rate/1200) - 1. This is an approximation of a rolling T-bill's total return, accurate to a few basis points, and is the only derived figure among the benchmark series.

title: MIT Response to Questions in the Letter dated January 24, 2008 of Senator Max Baucus and Senator Charles Grassley of the United States Senate Committee on Finance
page: Table 6A (Q6A, ten-year endowment values), Table 6C (Q6C, 2008 Target Allocations for Endowment), Table 10D (Q10D, Investment Return to the Endowment)
notes: MIT's own signed response to the Senate Finance Committee, dated March 3, 2008, published by the MIT News Office. THE ONLY MIT DOCUMENT FOUND THAT PUBLISHES AN ALLOCATION TABLE LABELLED FOR THE ENDOWMENT BEFORE FY2013: Table 6C, 'the allocation targets for investments in each asset class for the fiscal (academic) year ending June 30, 2008', headed '2008 Target Allocations for Endowment' - hence basis 'target' on the FY2008 rows. MIT's own caveat is printed beneath it: 'Actual investment in the above asset classes may vary from the target allocations at any given point in time.' Also the source for FY2000-FY2007 returns (Table 10D, 'Investment Return to the Endowment', an explicit ten-year series) and FY2000-FY2006 market values (Table 6A, 'Net Endowment Value at Year End'). Table 6A's own 'Net Endowment Growth (%)' column is NOT an investment return - MIT defines it as including gifts and spending - and is deliberately not used; FY2000 reads 51.0% growth against a 55.6% return.

title: MIT Response to Questions in the Letter of February 8, 2016 from Senator Orrin Hatch of the United States Senate Committee on Finance and Congressman Kevin Brady and Congressman Peter Roskam of the House Committee on Ways and Means
page: Table 1.2 (Endowment Asset Allocation, FY2013-FY2015), Table 2.1 (values at year end), Table 3.1 (net endowment value and net investment return, FY2008-FY2015)
notes: MIT's own signed response to the 2016 congressional endowment inquiry, dated April 1, 2016. THE ONLY MIT DOCUMENT FOUND THAT PUBLISHES ACTUAL (NOT TARGET) ENDOWMENT ALLOCATION PERCENTAGES: Table 1.2, headed 'Endowment Asset Allocation' with the column heading 'Asset Allocation as a Percentage of the Endowment' and columns 2015 / 2014 / 2013. Dating evidence that these are fiscal-year-end columns: the endowment values printed in the adjacent Tables 2.1 and 3.1 under the same year labels ($13,474.7M / $12,425.1M / $10,858.0M) equal MIT's June 30 endowment values in the Treasurer's Reports for FY2015 / FY2014 / FY2013 exactly. MIT states in the surrounding prose that about 98% of the endowment is invested through the unitized pool whose allocation the table shows, with about 2% held as non-cash gifts - the measurement-universe caveat in MIT's own words. Also the source for the FY2008 and FY2009 returns (3.2% and -17.1%), which MIT's Treasurer's Reports for those years do not state; Table 3.1 independently reproduces every FY2010-FY2015 return we curated from the Treasurer's Reports.
